chunks: Zakariyyā ibn Mālik al-Juʿfī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And know that whatever you gain, a fifth of it is for Allah, the Messenger, the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the traveler."

He said: "As for Allah's khums, it is for the Messenger, who places it in the way of Allah. As for the khums of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, it is for his relatives. And the khums of the near relatives means his close kin. And the orphans are the orphans of his Ahl al-Bayt, so He made these four shares among them. As for the needy and the sons of the road, you have known that we do not eat charity, nor is it lawful for us; so it is for the needy and the sons of the road."

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: his household, referring to the Prophet’s family
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: charity, which is stated here to be impermissible for Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْمَسَاكِينُ: the needy persons entitled to support
key_terms.الْيَتَامَىٰ: the orphans, here explained as the orphans of Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.خُمُسُ: the one-fifth share taken from gain
key_terms.ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ: the near relatives of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explain the khums verse in Surah al-Anfal?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the distribution of khums mentioned in the verse, identifying the shares connected to Allah, the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and Dhī al-Qurbā as designated for the Prophet’s family. It also clarifies that Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام do not take from ṣadaqah, and thus the categories of needy persons and wayfarers are treated distinctly in this explanation.
